findings.title: Table1 total reconciliation

findings.title: No test statistics reported
findings.description: statcheck recovered ZERO NHST statistics from the entire paper. This is not a tool failure -- it is an accurate description of the reporting. The paper contains no F statistic, no t statistic, no degrees of freedom and no exact p-value anywhere; every one of its several hundred inferential claims is carried by an asterisk in a table cell or a figure. The consequence is that no reported test statistic can be recalculated against its own p-value, and the only route to checking any claim is reconstruction from the group means and SDs, which is what the rivets_independent_t findings above do. Severity is `indeterminate` because nothing could be verified, NOT because the paper passed a check.

findings.notes: Run via check_table, which typed all 54 cells successfully (100% parse coverage, every cell mean_sd) and then dispatched to check_sd_or_se -- the only applicable check -- which refused on all 54. Two independent structural reasons. First, the outcome variables are continuous (withdrawal weight in grams, latency in seconds), which correctly bars GRIM, GRIMMER, SPRITE and DEBIT; applying them here would manufacture impossibilities out of ordinary measurements. Second, the paper never states an exact n for any cell, only the range '6-8 rats at each point', so even the dispersion check cannot be pinned. This is the denominator that matters for the whole review: 0 of 54 checks could run. The tables of this paper are by construction almost entirely immune to per-cell forensic arithmetic, and the significance-reconstruction route used elsewhere in this sweep is the only one available. The same reasoning applies unchanged to Tables 2, 4, 5 and 6, whose variables are likewise all continuous and whose footnotes state the same 6-8 range.

findings.title: Data availability withheld (Data Availability and Data Availability Statement sections)
findings.description: No data are deposited and no repository, accession or supplementary data file is named for a 348-animal study funded by multiple public bodies. Under rulebook rule 7 this is a state-but-withhold pattern. It is a weak signal on its own and is recorded as such; its relevance here is that it closes off the one route that could resolve the discrepancies found above -- the underlying per-animal values would settle the Table 1 accounting and every unreachable-p asterisk at once. The paper also supplies no supplementary materials of any kind, so no participant-level duplication analysis was possible.
